Then you can also edit the size of the zipper.  
Here you can select the number of zipper teeth.  
Then at the bottom, you can edit the total width of the zipper.  
That is, its zipper width.  
Here it is 1.2 cm.  
After editing the number, let's simulate it.  
You can see that the zipper will simulate  
the width of the zipper at the bottom,  
and it just fits well on the zipper.  
Then we can make some small changes.  
Next, we can sew the two ends of the zipper.  
After making the zipper,  
the handle of the zipper is on the two ends,  
and the zipper does not match with the button.  
So here we have a hole here.  
For convenience,  
we can change the rendering type of the clothing to the surface texture.  
Let's move the zipper to the bottom.  
Then we are at the bottom of the chain.  
Drag our board.  
Here you can see,  
it is actually an open state.  
Close the simulation while dragging the board.  
Then you can use the line sewing tool to sew.  
Use a pair of multi-sewing tools here.  
Click on the board first.  
Then press the Shift key without releasing it.  
Then click on the chain on one side.  
Click on the other side again.  
When clicking,  
please pay attention to the position and direction of the seam line.  
Finally, release the Shift key.  
Complete our sewing.  
Simulate.  
So our chain end is sewn together,  
and when pulling again,  
it will not open.  
When we encounter the two ends of the chain,  
there is less fabric,  
for example, like the upper end now.  
Then drag this chain and you will find  
it is more difficult to make a gap.  
This is not convenient to sew.  
At this time we can select the chain.  
Then in the attribute editor,  
find the option to sew the chain.  
Turn it off.  
Then simulate again.  
At this time the chain will be untied.  
Then just turn here lightly.  
You can see  
the fabric of the pocket  
and the fabric on both sides of our chain are separated.  
At this time select the sewing tool on the middle line.  
Click on the fabric of the pocket.  
Then press the Shift key.  
Click on the zipper on both sides.  
Pay attention to the position and direction of the click.  
Then press the Control button again  
for simulation.  
Complete the seam.  
After the zipper is done,  
you can adjust some appearance details.  
First select our zipper again.  
Open the zipper option again.  
Then select its opening.  
Change it to a closed opening.  
If the zipper is not in the opening,  
select the opening in the 3D window.  
Right-click to hide the opening.  
Below is the setting of the zipper type.  
Select the zipper.  
Then click on the top to preset.  
You can switch to different zipper types.  
Under the zipper,  
you can adjust your wrong way  
from the other side.  
You can also set the zipper to the lower edge  
and select many zipper types.  
We also use supporting parts  
to support the zipper,  
to find the right fit,  
and accordingly.  
Then you have the option to refer.

from the top of the zipper

Then you can select the bottom,  
follow the zipper,

chunks.content: # CLO Tips Mini-Class: Zipper Pocket Construction This document details the step-by-step process of constructing zipper pockets using CLO software. It covers panel arrangement, sewing techniques, zipper addition, parameter adjustments, and final finishing touches, focusing on industry-specific tools and commands within CLO. --- ## Panel Arrangement for Zipper Pockets This section explains how to arrange large and small pocket panels accurately in CLO, using positioning tools and alignment features for proper panel placement. - Combine large and small pocket panels as needed. - Use the **Quick Arrangement** button located at the upper right corner of the positioning ball to arrange pocket panels on the large panel. - Use the blue arrow on the positioning ball to drag the panel down without loosening left and right keys. - When moving the panel to the edge, a shadow appears indicating the stopping point, ensuring the pocket panel aligns correctly on the large panel. - For overall arrangement, select both the large and pocket panels simultaneously. - Open the arrangement points of the virtual model, then click the left button on the corresponding arrangement point to complete alignment. - Repeat this arrangement process for all remaining panels based on the garment structure. --- ## Sewing Pocket Panels and Zipper Pattern This section covers the use of sewing and collet tools to secure pocket panels and zipper patterns before simulation. - Select the **Collet Outline Tool**, then click on the base line of the pocket panel. - Click the **Return Car to Collet** to secure the outline. - Use the **Free Sewing Tool** to sew the pocket panel. - Repeat the collet outline process for the zipper pattern. - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool**, right-click on the internal pattern, and select **Convert to Move** to adjust parts. - Sew remaining parts following the garment’s normal construction sequence. - After sewing, simulate the garment to verify the pocket’s appearance. --- ## Adding Zipper Lines in 3D and 2D Windows This section explains how to add zipper lines using CLO’s 3D and 2D interfaces. - **3D Window Method:** - Select the collet outline tool. - Click the left button to start tracing the zipper line. - Follow the zipper path by sliding the mouse, then double-click to complete. - Repeat for the opposite side of the zipper. - **2D Window Method:** - Move the mouse to the 2D window. - Click the start button to begin. - Double-click to finish the zipper line. - Repeat for the other side. --- ## Adjusting Zipper Parameters This section details how to customize zipper dimensions and appearance using the property editor. - Select the **Move Tool**, then click the zipper. - In the **Property Editor**, modify: - Zipper length. - Zipper size. - Number of zipper teeth. - Total zipper width (e.g., 1.2 cm). - After adjustments, simulate to verify proper zipper fit and width.

chunks.content: - Double-click to finish the zipper line. - Repeat for the other side. --- ## Adjusting Zipper Parameters This section details how to customize zipper dimensions and appearance using the property editor. - Select the **Move Tool**, then click the zipper. - In the **Property Editor**, modify: - Zipper length. - Zipper size. - Number of zipper teeth. - Total zipper width (e.g., 1.2 cm). - After adjustments, simulate to verify proper zipper fit and width. --- ## Sewing Zipper Ends and Handling Chain Tension This section describes how to sew the zipper ends and manage fabric tension for realistic simulation. - The zipper handle appears on both ends, but may not align with button placement, causing a hole. - Change clothing rendering to **Surface Texture** for better visualization. - Move the zipper chain to the bottom and drag the board to an open state. - Use the **Line Sewing Tool** and multi-sewing technique: - Click on the board. - Hold the **Shift** key and click on one side of the zipper chain. - Click on the other side, ensuring seam line position and direction are correct. - Release **Shift** to complete sewing. - Simulate to confirm the chain end is sewn and does not open when pulled. - For zipper chain ends with less fabric (e.g., upper end), sewing can be difficult: - Select the chain and turn off the **Sew Chain** option in the attribute editor. - Simulate to allow the chain to untie and separate from pocket fabric. - Use the sewing tool on the middle line, click on pocket fabric, hold **Shift**, and click zipper on both sides. - Confirm seam line direction and position, then press **Control** for simulation to finalize sewing. --- ## Final Adjustments and Zipper Appearance Settings This section covers refining zipper settings and switching zipper types for improved realism. - Select the zipper and open zipper options. - Change zipper opening to **Closed Opening** for final appearance. - If the zipper is not visible in the opening, select the opening in the 3D window, right-click, and choose **Hide Opening**. - Adjust zipper type by selecting the zipper, clicking on the top preset, and switching between different zipper styles. - Additional settings include: - Adjusting zipper orientation (e.g., from the other side). - Positioning zipper to the lower edge. - Selecting supporting parts to fit and stabilize the zipper. - Choosing stitch reference points: top, middle, or bottom of the zipper. - Setting zipper side preferences (right or left). - Use the **Shy** and **Right Killed** options for further seam refinement. --- This concludes the detailed instructions for constructing zipper pockets in CLO, providing precise methods for panel arrangement, sewing, zipper addition, parameter customization, and final finishing to ensure functional and aesthetic zipper pockets.
